Nina Whitfield. I am a music supervisor, based in London. This is my first time working with a Brazilian team, so tell me what you actually do, and please skip the job title.
Pedro. I work between audiovisual production and music production, on music shows. The title is useless, so I usually say I make sure the music and the pictures arrive at the same second.
That is the best answer I have had all month. So you are the person who finds out, at eleven at night, that the cue is four seconds too long.
That is exactly it. And right now I am building the backing tracks for a new season, so this week I am in rehearsals every afternoon with a notebook.
Good. Then you already know the question I care about. On your show, who decides when a key is wrong for a singer? The musical director, the artist, or you?

Officially the musical director. In practice it happens in the rehearsal, and whoever hears it first says it. Half of the crew has been on this show since the first season, so nobody waits for permission.
I spent eleven years as a session singer before I moved to this side of the glass, so I know that room very well. The best show I worked on was the one where the runner was allowed to say something.
Then you understand why I keep the third take and not the first. The first one is always the one where everybody is being polite.
Say that again in the meeting on Thursday and you will have the room. One last thing: do you do anything outside the show? I ask everybody, and the answer is usually the interesting one.
On the side, I produce my own projects, and I am studying songwriting. And you, what are you working on at the moment?

Welcome to the course. Before the first class, here is how this one works, because it is not a lecture. Every week you bring something. It can be eight bars, it can be a single verse, it can be a rough voice memo recorded on your phone at two in the morning. You post it, and the rest of the group listens to it before we meet. Then, in the live session, we talk about it. And I mean talk. I am going to ask you what the song is trying to do, and you are going to answer in your own words, out loud, in front of eleven strangers. That part frightens people, so let me be honest about it. Nobody here is grading your accent. What we are listening for is whether you can say why you made a choice. If you can tell me why the second verse is shorter than the first, you are doing exactly what this course asks for. Every week somebody says, my English is not good enough for this. And every week that person turns out to be the one with the most interesting reason.

People ask what I do and I still do not have a clean answer, so I usually give them the long one. I sit between two departments. On one side there is the picture, the cameras, the edit, the show going out on a Sunday night. On the other side there is the music, the band, the arrangements, the backing tracks the singers perform over. My job is the place where those two things have to agree. Right now, for example, I am working on a new season, and this week that means three things at the same time. I am building the backing tracks for the live shows. I am sitting in rehearsals with a notebook, because that is where you find out that a key is wrong for somebody. And I am on the phone with the picture team about a cue that runs four seconds long. None of that appears in a job title. So when somebody at a party asks me what I do, I say I make sure the music and the pictures arrive at the same second. It is not the whole truth, but it is the part that makes sense to a stranger in ten words.

Pedro works between audiovisual production and music production. He works on music shows: The Voice, Masked Singer and X Factor. Right now he is building the backing tracks for a new season. This week he is also sitting in rehearsals with the band. On the side, he produces his own projects. Then he asks the other person what they are working on at the moment.
